name: binary_load
title: Load a binary
description: Load a binary for analysis: an ELF file under a root, a raw blob, the built-in demo or an open binary by its ID. Send exactly one of path, builtin and binary_id. A relative path starts at the first root of the server, and a path outside the roots gives PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT. Send file_format raw and base for a blob of x86-64 code. The analysis runs after the load within max_steps. The result gives the binary_id for later calls, and already_loaded tells if the binary is open already.

path.description: The path of the file. A relative path starts at the first root of the server.

builtin.description: The name of a built-in binary. The demo binary is a small password check.

binary_id.description: The ID of a binary that is open in the session, or of a project on disk.

file_format.description: The file format. The value auto lets the probe find the format.

arch.description: The machine of a raw blob.

base.description: The load address of a raw blob, as a 0x hex string.

entry.description: The entry address of a raw blob, as a 0x hex string.

analysis.description: How far the analysis runs after the load.

format.description: The detail level. The detailed form adds provenance, coercion details and sizes.

fields.description: JSON pointers into data. The result keeps only these fields.

max_chars.description: The largest result in characters. The count includes every copy of the result.

session.description: The session label for provenance, filters and the undo scope.

expected_rev.description: The rev that the call expects. Another rev gives CONFLICT.

dry_run.description: Return the planned edit list with no commit.

max_steps.description: The fuel of the call in work units.

max_ms.description: A wall-clock guard in milliseconds. Fuel stays the main stop rule.

name: binary_survey
title: Survey a binary
description: Survey a loaded binary: identity, protections, sections, imports, strings, entry points, functions, syscalls and coverage. Call it first after binary_load. Each section gets a part of max_chars. When a section does not fit, its member omitted gives the count of the items that it leaves out and a search call for them. Imports come in groups by capability category, and strings show the most referenced strings first. Send include to get fewer sections.

include.description: The sections of the survey in output order. The default is all 14 sections.

binary_id.description: The ID of the target binary. Leave it out when exactly one binary is open.

format.description: The detail level. The detailed form adds provenance, coercion details and sizes.

fields.description: JSON pointers into data. The result keeps only these fields.

max_chars.description: The largest result in characters. The count includes every copy of the result.

session.description: The session label for provenance, filters and the undo scope.

name: analysis_run
title: Run the analysis
description: Run or resume the analysis of a binary within a fuel budget. The run stops at a fixpoint or after max_steps work units. The state complete means that no analyzer has work. The state budget_stopped means that reads see a partial set, so call analysis_run again while resume is true. The state stale means that a re-analysis runs, and reads see the old set. The result lists each analyzer with its priority band, its pending ranges and its runs, and the changed facts of the call.

until.description: How far the analysis runs. The value triage stops after band 700.

binary_id.description: The ID of the target binary. Leave it out when exactly one binary is open.

format.description: The detail level. The detailed form adds provenance, coercion details and sizes.

name: func_list
title: List the functions
description: List and filter the functions of a binary, and sort them by address, name, size or priority. Each item gives the ID, the entry, the name, the size, the start reason, the confidence, the counts of callers and callees, and the caveats. The sort priority puts functions with risky imports, many references and strings first. Each analysis run fixes the priority order, so names and visits do not change it. Send filter to narrow the list, and cursor for the next page.

name.description: A glob for the name, for example parse_*.

start_reason.description: Keep the functions with one of these start reasons.

visited.description: Keep the functions that a func_get call read, or the others.

named.description: Keep the functions with a real name, or the functions with a default name.

typed.description: Keep the functions with a signature, or the others.

has_caveat.description: Keep the functions with a caveat, or the others.

calls.description: A glob for the name of an import that the function calls, for example recv*.

filter.description: The filters. A function must pass every filter of the object.

sort.description: The order of the list. The value priority gives the most interesting functions first.

binary_id.description: The ID of the target binary. Leave it out when exactly one binary is open.

format.description: The detail level. The detailed form adds provenance, coercion details and sizes.

fields.description: JSON pointers into data. The result keeps only these fields.

max_chars.description: The largest result in characters. The count includes every copy of the result.

limit.description: The largest number of items on one page.

cursor.description: The page.next_cursor of the previous page.

count_only.description: Return only the count of the items.

shape.description: The form of the items. The table form gives cols and rows.

in.description: Keep only the members of this named set, for example set:parsers.

session.description: The session label for provenance, filters and the undo scope.

name: func_get
title: Get functions
description: Get one or more functions with selected sections: summary, disassembly, IR, decompiled C, xrefs, callers, callees, strings, variables, notes, why, CFG and jump tables. Send target, or targets for up to 50 functions. The sections share max_chars by weight, so a large section can come back cut. A cut disassembly or decompile gives next_cursor: send it in cursors to read on. decomp_opts.lines selects a window of lines of the decompiled C, and ir_opts.level l1 gives the SSA form. The member omitted names each section that did not fit, with its size. A call with disasm, ir or decomp marks the function as visited, and this mark changes no fact.

target.description: The function: an address in its body, a name or a fn: ID.

targets.description: Up to 50 functions. Each item gets its own result.

include.description: The sections to return in this order.

level.description: The IR level: l0 for the lifted ops, l1 for the SSA form after the passes.

ir_opts.description: The options of the ir section.

start.description: The number of the first line, from 1.

lines.description: The window of lines to return.

fold.description: Put each value with one use into its use.

sailr.description: Run the SAILR-lite passes: canary removal, noreturn calls and tail calls.

canary.description: Remove the stack canary check. It needs sailr.

tailcall.description: Show a tail jump as return f(..). It needs sailr.

passes.description: The decompiler passes to turn on or off.

decomp_opts.description: The options of the decomp section: the window of lines and the passes.

disasm_limit.description: The largest number of disassembly rows.

disasm.description: The disasm.next_cursor of the previous call.

ir.description: The ir.next_cursor of the previous call.

decomp.description: The decomp.next_cursor of the previous call.

cursors.description: The section cursors of the previous call, to get the next rows of a section.

binary_id.description: The ID of the target binary. Leave it out when exactly one binary is open.

format.description: The detail level. The detailed form adds provenance, coercion details and sizes.

fields.description: JSON pointers into data. The result keeps only these fields.

name: xref_list
title: List cross-references

The target imp:puts gives every site of the import, and `via` tells the path: plt, got or direct. Send direction from for the references out of a function body. Send args true for the argument values of each call: an integer, a string, a function, an address or unknown. When basis.complete is false, an unresolved indirect call can add callers.

direction.description: The value to lists the references to the targets. The value from lists the references from them.

kinds.description: Keep only these classes of references.

depth.description: The depth of the call graph in edges. A depth above 1 adds the call edges of each level.

max_nodes.description: The largest number of functions in edges.

context.description: The number of instructions before each site to show.

args.description: Add the argument values of each call site.

name: search
title: Search a binary
description: Search the items of a binary by kind: names, strings, bytes, comments, notes, types, imports, exports, sections, segments, libraries, symbols, sets and jump tables. Send kind with a query, or ids with note:, set: or jt: IDs to read full records. An empty query lists every item of the kind. The match substr ignores the letter case. In a byte pattern, two question marks match any byte. String items give the reference count and a call that lists the references.

items.description: A note:, set: or jt: ID.

match.description: How the query matches: a part of the text, a glob or the exact text.

pattern.description: The byte pattern in hex, for example 48 8b ?? 4?. The mark ?? matches any byte.

section.description: Keep the items in the section with this name.

perms.description: Keep the items in regions with all of these permissions, for example rx.

name: calc
title: Calculate values
description: Calculate numbers and addresses: bases, widths, signedness and file offsets. The expression takes the operators + - * / % << >> & | ^ ~ and parentheses. A term is a 0x hex number, a symbol, a section name, a default name such as FUN_00401000 or an ID such as fn:0x401000. A term of digits only is an error, because the server does not guess the base. The arithmetic uses 64 bits and wraps, and division is unsigned. With an open binary, the result also tells the region, the file offset and the function at the value.

description: List the history of edits since a revision, and the analysis runs. The rows come from the journal of the project, so old rows stay. By default each changed fact gives one row with its last rev and session. Send coalesce false for one row per edit with its transaction and undone_by. Send session to keep one session, or exclude_session to leave one out. Call it after a context reset to see what changed since your last rev.

exclude_session.description: Leave out the commits of this session label.

coalesce.description: Give one row per changed fact with its last change. Send false for one row per edit.
